newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle sales thin, $68, dn $1 -trade.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle sales thin, $68, dn $1 -trade.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle sold at $68.00 per cwt in light volume Wednesday afternoon, down $1.00 from last week's top price, feedlot sources and USDA reported.
About 4,700 head sold in Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma, USDA confirmed, with no sales reported in Kansas.
Packers were seen lowering bids to $67.00 Thursday amid ideas the light sales at $68.00 would spur further declines, some sources said.
Packers bid $68.00 through the day, with owners generally passing the bids and asking $70.00 to $71.00.
Fed cattle prices this week had been projected to be steady to firmer compared with last week's top of $69.00, but beef prices began to slip which eroded optimism for higher cattle values, they said.
Beef prices on Wednesday were quoted down $0.28 to $0.88 per cwt on 308 fabricated loads reported sold, USDA said.
Choice heavyweight beef was quoted down $0.28 at $107.51 at Wednesday's close, following Tuesday's advance to the highest level in almost three months, since December 10.
